answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before receiving a daily job quota. Whether agents map a meadow, monitor an ocean, or summarize a discussion thread, each account needs its own deposit. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, costing the attacker liquidity and foregone returns. Splitting one balance among aliases cannot multiply the quota without multiplying the locked capital.
